text: bro what the oracle is for the shit i dont need to reexplain over and over again, by not doing it now, your going to make it end up there by the next time you call it
resolution: Corrected where the skinning decision was filed. The user's point: the oracle exists so they do not have to re-explain things, and by recording their skinning rationale only in a memory file and the agent-seat skill doc — both places only the assistant reads — I guaranteed they would have to say it again the next time anyone consulted the oracle on model semantics. Ruled it into the constitution instead as V33 (SEMBLOB-0801): semantic region names are RIGGING DATA, not agent scratch memory, because named surfaces are what make auto-skinning from a UV tractable, and therefore the semantic table must persist into the model blob rather than living only as host state a cold restart drops. Two standing consequences are written in so future work does not need re-litigation: any model-persistence work (meshdoc/blob save+load) carries the semantic table through as in-scope rather than optional, and any authoring surface that creates geometry (Agent Seat, outliner, importers, primitive adds) names what it creates at the moment of creation, since a name reconstructed later from normals is a guess. The verdict also states that an op which resets or drops the semantic table is a BUG rather than an acceptable cost, citing the add-verb table wipe (req_3588) and its part-range twin (req_3465) as the same disease. Both the user's original verbatim words and their correction are quoted in the verdict so the reasoning survives without them. Updated DECISIONS.md and _index/decisions.ts in the same commit per the maintenance contract, and verified the oracle now returns V33 ranked top for semantics/skinning/persistence queries. The verdict records honestly that the persistence half is OWED, not built — names remain live-only host state today. Staged only the two doc files: a parallel session is concurrently adding persist/detachSelection to seatApi.ts and that work was left untouched.
